name: Cerebrolysin

lead: Cerebrolysin is an injectable mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and amino acids prepared from porcine brain protein. It is approved in many countries for stroke, traumatic brain injury and dementia. In forum threads on iqmaxxing and brainmaxxing, members use it hoping for sharper studying and exam performance.

Preclinical studies report it mimics neurotrophic factor activity and promotes neurogenesis in rodent stroke and Alzheimer models, including through the Sonic hedgehog pathway. Human trials are in neurological patients, including the CARS trial in post-stroke recovery and a meta-analysis of nine randomized trials. Its effect in healthy people has not been studied, and one small registered study listed hair repigmentation during therapy.

paras: Clinically it is given by injection or infusion in courses under medical supervision. Forum members discuss it as a nootropic stack addition.
It is an animal-derived injectable and a prescription product where approved. Members mention obtaining it from unofficial sources, which carries quality and sterility concerns.

angle.text: Cerebrolysin is discussed as an iqmaxxing nootropic for sharper study performance, building on trials in stroke and dementia. It is not an appearance compound.

lead: Cerebrolysin is a mixture of low-molecular-weight peptides and free amino acids produced by enzymatic breakdown of porcine brain proteins, described as mimicking neurotrophic factors [1][2]. It is manufactured by EVER Neuro Pharma in Austria and given by injection or infusion [1].

It is approved in many countries for neurological conditions such as stroke, traumatic brain injury and dementia [1]. Human trials have been conducted in post-stroke recovery, including the CARS randomized trial and a meta-analysis of nine randomized trials [3][4].
In looksmaxxing communities it is discussed as a cognitive enhancer. No trial has examined it for appearance outcomes; one small registered study listed hair repigmentation during therapy [5].

paras: Laboratory studies in rats reported that Cerebrolysin increased neurogenesis after experimental stroke and improved functional outcome [6], and that the Sonic hedgehog pathway mediated this effect [7]. A review describes it as a neuropeptide preparation that mimics endogenous neurotrophic factors and, in dementia models, reduces beta-amyloid deposition and tau phosphorylation [2].

The CARS trial randomized stroke patients to Cerebrolysin or saline for 21 days and assessed upper-limb motor function at day 90 [3]. A meta-analysis of nine randomized trials examined its safety and efficacy in early post-stroke recovery [4], and an Asian double-blind trial studied acute ischemic stroke [8]. Registered trials listed include stroke, traumatic brain injury, Down syndrome and preterm infants [9][10][11]. A 5-person registered study examined hair repigmentation during Cerebrolysin therapy [5]. No studies found in healthy people for cognitive enhancement or for appearance outcomes.

Looksmax.org threads include a member considering it before an entrance exam, a thread titled as a deep dive into "iqmaxxing", and others asking about "brainmaxx" use [12][13][14][15]. Members debate whether nootropics in general are "cope".
